blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Definition : The total living factor (biotic) and total non-living factor (abiotic) of the environment present in a particular area is called an ecosystem.
A.G.Tansley - The term "ecosystem" first of all coined by A.G. Tansley.
According to Tansley - The ecosystem is a symbol of the structure and function of nature.
E.P. Odum - Father of ecosystem ecology.
According to E.P. Odum - Ecosystem is the smallest structural and functional unit of nature or environment.

blocks.prompt: The term ecosystem was coined by :-

blocks.title: Question- 2
blocks.question:
Which ecosystem has the maximum biomass?

(1) Grassland ecosystem

(2) Pond ecosystem

(3) Lake ecosystem

(4) Forest ecosystem
blocks.answer:
Ans- 4

Forests, especially tropical rainforests, have the highest biomass among ecosystems. This is because they contain a large number of plants and trees, which are capable of storing significant amounts of energy in the form of biomass. The high primary productivity in forest ecosystems leads to a large amount of energy being captured and stored by producers (plants).

blocks.title: Question- 3
blocks.question:
A soil is said to be fertile when -

(1) It is rich in organic matter

(2) It has capacity to hold water

(3) It has a capacity to hold nutrients

(4) It holds water & all essential nutrients in a definite proportion
blocks.answer:
Ans- 4

Fertile soil is characterized by its ability to retain an adequate amount of water, while also providing all the necessary nutrients that plants need in the right proportions. This balance is crucial for supporting healthy plant growth. Fertile soil typically contains a good mix of organic matter, minerals, and microorganisms, and it also has the ability to retain moisture while allowing excess water to drain properly.
options: (1) It is rich in organic matter
(2) It has capacity to hold water
(3) It has a capacity to hold nutrients
(4) It holds water & all essential nutrients in a definite proportion

blocks.title: Question:1
blocks.question:
In the equation GPP-R NPP GPP is Gross Primary Productivity NPP is the Net Primary Productivity R here is:

(1) Respiratory quotient

(2) Respiratory loss

(3) Reproductive allocation

(4) Photosynthetically active radiation
blocks.answer:
Ans: (2)

In the equation GPP - R = NPP,

  • GPP (Gross Primary Productivity) refers to the total amount of energy captured by plants through photosynthesis.
  • R represents the respiratory loss, which is the energy used by plants for their own metabolic processes (like respiration).
  • NPP (Net Primary Productivity) is the energy available for growth and reproduction of plants after subtracting the energy lost through respiration.

blocks.title: Question:2
blocks.question:
In relation of Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity of an ecosystem, which one of the following statements is correct?

(1) There is no relationship between Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity.

(2) Gross primary productivity is always less than net primary productivity.

(3) Gross primary productivity is always more than net primary productivity.

(4) Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity are one and same.
blocks.answer:
Ans: (3)

Gross primary productivity (GPP) is the total amount of energy captured by plants through photosynthesis. Net primary productivity (NPP) is the energy remaining after subtracting the energy plants use for their own respiration (R). Since plants use some of the energy they capture for respiration, NPP is always less than GPP. Therefore, GPP is always greater than NPP.
options: (1) There is no relationship between Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity.
(2) Gross primary productivity is always less than net primary productivity.
(3) Gross primary productivity is always more than net primary productivity.
(4) Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity are one and same.

blocks.title: Question:2
blocks.question:
In an ecosystem the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis is termed as :-

(1) Gross primary productivity

(2) Secondary productivity

(3) Net productivity

(4) Net primary productivity
blocks.answer:
Ans:(1)

Gross primary productivity (GPP) refers to the total rate at which energy is captured by producers (typically plants) during photosynthesis to produce organic matter. This is the overall energy input into the ecosystem before accounting for energy losses due to respiration by producers.

blocks.title: Ecological Pyramid
blocks.text:
In most ecosystems, all the pyramids of number, energy and biomass are upright. There are exceptions to this generalisation:

(i) If we count the number of insects feeding on a big tree, we get an inverted pyramid.

(ii) Now, if we add an estimate of the number of small birds depending on the insects as well as the number of larger birds eating the smaller ones, We get a spindle-shaped pyramid.

(iii) The pyramid of biomass in the sea is generally inverted because the biomass of fishes far exceeds that of phytoplanktons.

blocks.title: Points to Remember
blocks.text:
Limitations of ecological pyramids:

  • It does not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels.
  • It assumes a simple food chain, something that almost never exists in nature; it does not accommodate a food web.
  • Saprophytes are not given any place.

blocks.title: Question: 1
blocks.question:
The amount of nutrients such as carbon, nitrogen, potassium and calcium present in the soil at any given time is referred to as:
(1) Standing state
(2) Standing crop
(3) Humus
(4) Detritus
blocks.answer:
Ans: (1)

The standing state refers to the amount of nutrients, such as carbon, nitrogen, potassium, and calcium, present in the soil at any given time. It represents the nutrient content available for organisms in the ecosystem, and it can be affected by various factors, including the type of soil, vegetation, and the nutrient cycles.

blocks.title: Question: 2
blocks.question:
The upright pyramid of numbers is absent in:

(1) Lake

(2) Grassland

(3) Pond

(4) Forest
blocks.answer:
Ans- 4

In a forest ecosystem, the pyramid of numbers is often inverted or not upright. This is because forests tend to have a large number of smaller organisms like insects and herbivores at lower trophic levels, but a relatively smaller number of larger organisms (like trees) at the higher trophic levels. As a result, the biomass of producers (trees) can be much greater than that of primary consumers (herbivores), leading to an inverted pyramid of numbers in terms of individual organisms.

In contrast, ecosystems like lakes, grasslands, and ponds often have upright pyramids of numbers where the number of individuals decreases as you move up trophic levels.

blocks.title: Question: 3
blocks.question:
Which one of the following statements for a pyramid of energy is incorrect, whereas the remaining three are correct?

(1) Its base is broad

(2) It shows the energy content of different trophic-level organisms

(3) It is inverted in shape

(4) It is upright in shape
blocks.answer:
Ans- 3

A pyramid of energy is typically upright in shape, meaning that energy decreases as you move up through the trophic levels (from producers to primary consumers, secondary consumers, etc.). The broad base represents the producers, which capture the most energy, while the apex of the pyramid represents the higher trophic levels that capture less energy.
options: (2) It shows the energy content of different trophic-level organisms
